exact_statement: For every Boolean seed g on m>=0 uniform core coordinates X, r control coordinates Z, and final physical edit mask E, put F(x,z)=g(x)(-1)^1_E(x,z). Assume every core fiber E_x has at most k assignments, k>=1 and k2^-r<=1/4. Let I_Z and I_X be the final F control/core influence sums, and Q=H(F)-E_z H(F_z), with entropy in bits. Then Q <= K I_Z+2 I_X, K=4r/(r-log2 k)+2/ln2. The core reserve is allocated once to the combined mask; I_X(F)>=I_X(1-2*1_E)>=2 P(E)log2(1/P_X(E_x nonempty)). Empty edit sets have Q=I_Z=0. In particular k=1,r>=2 gives K=4+2/ln2 and k=2,r>=3 gives K<=6+2/ln2. Two graph-controlled events with arbitrary shared core/domains/control maps have <=2 assignments per fiber after either XOR or union-once editing. Every complete physical control-reveal tree has this access price and retains all actual core leaves. If every complete leaf satisfies U<=bI, b>=0, the reviewed local granularity certificate gives H(F)<=max(K,4+2b)I(F). For earlier control-only stopping trees with U-certified leaves, the valid bound is H(F)<=(K+2+2b)I(F), retaining remaining control influence. No arbitrary core-leaf admission is asserted. Dropping the sparse-fiber cap invalidates the ownership inequality: g=(-1)^x and E={(0,0),(1,1)} on one core and one control bit give I_X(F)=0<I_X(1-2*1_E)=1.
hypotheses: Actual Boolean signs on finite uniform cubes; entropy in bits; standard physical pivotal influence.
The seed g is independent of the r control coordinates; the edit mask is the actual final physical XOR or union mask.
Every fiber has cardinality <=k and k2^-r<=1/4; this implies r>=2 and r-log2 k>0.
The full access tree exposes every control and retains the exact actual core restrictions; its reserve is not renewed at descendants.
The U conditions are hypotheses for terminal entropy payment, not consequences of the access bound.
